notes.front: What is an impediment in Scrum, in one sentence?
notes.back: Anything that blocks or slows the Scrum Team’s progress.
notes.explanation: The Scrum Guide uses the word without defining it: Daily Scrums identify impediments, and the Scrum Master causes their removal.
notes.example: Like a missing access badge that stops a new Developer from working for a week.

notes.front: The Developers are always accountable for creating a plan for the Sprint, the {{c1::Sprint Backlog}}.
notes.explanation: One of the four things the Developers are always accountable for.

notes.front: The Developers are always accountable for instilling quality by adhering to a {{c1::Definition of Done}}.
notes.explanation: One of the four things the Developers are always accountable for.

notes.front: The Developers are always accountable for adapting their plan each day toward the {{c1::Sprint Goal}}.
notes.explanation: One of the four things the Developers are always accountable for.

notes.front: The Developers are always accountable for holding each other accountable as {{c1::professionals}}.
notes.explanation: One of the four things the Developers are always accountable for.

notes.front: In Product Backlog management, the Product Owner develops and explicitly communicates the {{c1::Product Goal}}.
notes.explanation: One of four parts of effective Product Backlog management the Product Owner is accountable for.

notes.front: In Product Backlog management, the Product Owner creates and clearly communicates {{c1::Product Backlog items}}.
notes.explanation: One of four parts of effective Product Backlog management the Product Owner is accountable for.

notes.front: In Product Backlog management, the Product Owner {{c1::orders}} Product Backlog items.
notes.explanation: One of four parts of effective Product Backlog management the Product Owner is accountable for.

notes.front: In Product Backlog management, the Product Owner ensures the Product Backlog is {{c1::transparent, visible and understood}}.
notes.explanation: One of four parts of effective Product Backlog management the Product Owner is accountable for.

notes.front: Can the Product Owner delegate Product Backlog management work to others?
notes.back: Yes, but the Product Owner remains accountable.
notes.explanation: The Product Owner may do the work or delegate it; either way, the accountability stays with them.

notes.front: How can someone who wants to change the Product Backlog do so?
notes.back: By trying to convince the Product Owner.
notes.explanation: The Product Owner may represent the needs of many stakeholders in the Product Backlog.

notes.front: Whom does the Scrum Master serve?
notes.back: The Scrum Team, the Product Owner and the organisation.
notes.explanation: The Scrum Guide lists ways the Scrum Master serves each of the three.

notes.front: The Scrum Master serves the Scrum Team by causing the removal of {{c1::impediments}} to its progress.
notes.explanation: “Causing the removal” means making sure it happens, not necessarily doing it personally.

notes.front: The Scrum Master ensures that all Scrum events take place and are positive, productive and kept within the {{c1::timebox}}.
notes.explanation: One of the ways the Scrum Master serves the Scrum Team.

notes.front: The Scrum Master coaches team members in {{c1::self-management and cross-functionality}}.
notes.explanation: One of the ways the Scrum Master serves the Scrum Team.

notes.front: The Scrum Master serves the Product Owner by helping find techniques for effective {{c1::Product Goal definition and Product Backlog management}}.
notes.explanation: One of the ways the Scrum Master serves the Product Owner.

notes.front: The Scrum Master serves the organisation by removing barriers between {{c1::stakeholders and Scrum Teams}}.
notes.explanation: One of the ways the Scrum Master serves the organisation.

notes.front: Who is accountable for creating a valuable, useful Increment every Sprint?
notes.explanation: Within the Scrum Team, Scrum also defines three specific accountabilities: the Developers, the Product Owner and the Scrum Master.

notes.front: When a large Scrum Team reorganises into several Scrum Teams on the same product, what do they share?
notes.back: The same Product Goal, Product Backlog and Product Owner.
notes.explanation: Each team stays focused on the same product.

notes.front: What does the Scrum Guide say about implementing only parts of Scrum?
notes.back: It is possible, but the result is not Scrum.
notes.explanation: Scrum exists only in its entirety, and works well as a container for other techniques.

notes.front: A company runs Sprints and Daily Scrums but has dropped the Sprint Retrospective and has no Product Owner. Is it doing Scrum?
notes.back: No. Implementing only parts of Scrum is possible, but the result is not Scrum.
notes.explanation: Leaving out elements covers up problems and limits the benefits of Scrum, says the Scrum Guide.
notes.source: The Scrum Guide (November 2020), “Purpose of the Scrum Guide”

notes.front: The Developers have waited two weeks for a test environment from another department. Whose role includes causing this impediment’s removal?
notes.choices:
A) The Scrum Master
B) The Product Owner, by reordering the Product Backlog
C) Nobody: the team waits
notes.choicesExplained: B: the Product Owner orders the Product Backlog; causing the removal of impediments is one of the ways the Scrum Master serves the team. C: the Scrum Master serves the team by causing the removal of impediments to its progress, so waiting is not the answer.
notes.explanation: The Scrum Master need not remove it personally, but makes sure it is removed.

notes.front: A stakeholder tells a Developer to put a new item at the top of the Product Backlog. What should happen?
notes.back: The stakeholder tries to convince the Product Owner, who orders the Product Backlog.
notes.explanation: For Product Owners to succeed, the entire organisation must respect their decisions.

notes.front: At the Daily Scrum, a Developer says a supplier’s broken system is blocking their work. What is this called in Scrum?
notes.explanation: Daily Scrums help identify impediments, and the Scrum Master causes their removal.
